subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Power of Listening
description: One-minute skill: The Power of Listening.

hook.text: A study found that after a conversation, people rate the best listener as the most intelligent person present.

buildup.text: Most people wait to speak instead of listening. They rehearse their next point while the other person talks.

discovery.text: Active listening means reflecting back: 'So you're saying the project stalled because of budget cuts?' confirms understanding.

twist.text: Silence after someone finishes speaking is powerful. It signals you're processing, not rushing to respond.

climax.text: Ask follow-up questions that build on what they said. This proves you listened and deepens the conversation.

punchline.text: Listen to understand, not to reply. Ask, reflect, go deeper.

quiz.question: What makes someone perceived as a great listener?
options: Nodding frequently and maintaining constant eye contact
Reflecting back what was said and asking follow-up questions
Letting the other person talk without interruption
